evidence: Version 2 delivers the declared 'Nacre Twin-Disc Tide' concept as a finished campaign: the mother-of-pearl wall sweeps into a continuous matching nacre ground at a believable baseline, the right half stays a quiet cool grey that carries a clean editorial column (wide-tracked BVLGARI at column top, two-line narrow sans title, thin tide-line rule at column base), and the product sits left of column with matched soft high-key light. Against version 1, its typography is more coherent and legible because the背景 swirl is calmed behind the type, the horizon and ground contact read more stable, and there is no studio equipment or floating-packshot artifact. Version 1's busier marbled swirl competes with the title block and its sparkle hotspots break the controlled matte-nacre material, so version 2 is the stronger finished poster within this concept.
remaining_problems: Contact shadow under the bottle is a thin flat dark strip rather than a shadow that sinks into the shell-inlay seams; physical contact is plausible but not fully convinced.
The nacre wall reads as faint marbled texture rather than distinct mother-of-pearl shell chips in a vortex inlay; the iridescent sheen drift across facets is very subdued.
Title sets in a plain grotesque rather than a distinctly narrow column face, so the etched-label character of the two-line title is only partially achieved.
Ground plane is smooth and near-featureless near the base, weakening the continuous shell-inlay material story at the contact point.
